## 0.9.1 (2026-11-26)

**Wide files: every dataset ready to map.** The build now writes, next to each panel, the same data wide: `data/<dataset>/<scale>/<dataset>_wide.gpkg` and `_wide.geojson`, one row per unit with its name, the province and department it lies in, its source keys and area, and every variable once per year, `<variable>_<year>` (a column for every year of the dataset, empty where a variable has no values). The GeoPackage carries the analysis boundaries and a table `variables` describing every column (label, description, unit, source, actual reference year); the GeoJSON carries lighter boundaries for web maps (`wide_geojson_boundaries` in `project.yaml`). The observatory's website offers both for download.

- `geo.load(dataset, wide=True)` returns that table (with `geometry=True`, `years=` and `variables=`). `wide="<variable>"` is unchanged and keeps its names (`<variable><year>`).
- Building: `publish_wide()` writes the files and records them in the resource (`geo:gpkg`, `geo:geojson`); `write_docs()` runs it and lists the files in the README. Rebuilding unchanged data writes the same bytes.
- Validation: `validate` checks that both files are there and hold the panel's values, and that the GeoPackage describes every column.

## 0.9.0 (2026-11-26)

**Breaking: one folder per dataset.** Every dataset of the observatory now has a folder of its own, `data/<dataset>/`, that says how it is organised: its metadata (`datapackage.json`), its documentation (`README.md`, which GitHub shows when the folder is opened) and one subfolder per map with the panel (`data/sdg01/map343/sdg01.csv` and `.parquet`). `data/index.json` lists the datasets. The observatory's website links each dataset to its folder. Released versions up to 0.8.1 read the metadata from `metadata/` on `main`, which is gone: upgrade, or pin the data with `ref="v0.8.1"`.

- **The package reads the new layout**: `metadata.package_path()`, `metadata.INDEX` (`data/index.json`). Files are still found through each resource's `geo:path` and `geo:parquet`, now `data/<dataset>/<scale>/<dataset>.csv` and `.parquet`.
- **`emb` and `embpw` are one dataset, `emb`**: the area-weighted dimensions keep their names (`A00`–`A63`) and the population-weighted ones are `A00_pw`–`A63_pw`. `geo.load("embpw")` no longer works: use `geo.load("emb")` and the `_pw` columns.
- **`geo.cite()` lists the original sources first, then the observatory**, which processes and maintains the data (`citation` in `project.yaml`), then the other sources (boundaries, intermediaries), one APA citation per paragraph. `style="bibtex"` gives the observatory's BibTeX entry, with the same list as comments. `geo.info()` shows the same list, and the new `metadata.citations()` returns it. The per-dataset `geo:citation` is no longer used by the observatory's datasets; a dataset saved with `geo.save(..., citation=)` is cited with its own citation in the observatory's place.
- **`geo.save()` writes the same layout**: `<directory>/data/<name>/` with `datapackage.json`, a `README.md` (variables, files, citations) and `<scale>/<name>.csv` and `.parquet`. Its `sources` are cited first (`geo:role: original` unless a dict says otherwise).
- **Building**: `write_docs()` writes `data/<dataset>/README.md`, with the folder's layout and a Cite section in the order above; `write_catalog()` links the dataset folders.
- **Validation**: `validate` checks that each dataset's files sit in its folder, that its README exists, that `data/index.json` and the folders agree, and that nothing is left of `metadata/` or `docs/datasets/`.
- **Licenses**: SDSN Bolivia now licenses the Atlas de los ODS en Bolivia 2026 and its municipal map of 2025 under CC BY 4.0; the metadata, `geo.info()` and the docs say so.

## 0.8.1 (2026-11-21)

**Building: a finishing step for the data repository.** `geo4bolivia build` now ends by calling `after_build(target)` when the data repository's `builders/__init__.py` defines it, after the catalog. The observatory uses it to give every Python block of the generated dataset docs a Colab notebook of its own, so their Open in Colab badges open the code ready to run, as the website's code boxes do. Nothing changes for builders that do not define it.

## 0.8.0 (2026-11-21)

**Breaking: municipal maps are named by their units, and every spatial function knows its map.** The observatory now publishes two municipal maps that share their geo IDs: `map343`, SDSN Bolivia's map of 2025 (the SDG Atlas), and `map339`, the map of 2015 on whose polygons `pop`, `ntl`, `emb` and `embpw` were computed. A municipal ID alone no longer tells the map, so the map is recorded with the data and can be named in every call.

- **The scale `municipality` is now `map343`**, in every function (`geo.units("map343")`, `geo.boundaries("map343")`, `scale="map343"`) and in the published paths (`data/map343/sdg.csv`, `geo/boundaries/map343.geojson`). `"municipality"` raises an error that lists the known scales.
- **New scale `map339`.** `pop`, `ntl`, `emb` and `embpw` are published on it, with all 339 municipalities of 2015 (instead of 333 on the 2025 map); `geo.crosswalk("map339", "map343")` gives the area shares between the two maps.
- **`map=`** on every function that draws or uses boundaries: `weights`, `connectivity`, `moran`, `lisa`, `map`, `beta_convergence`, `convergence_clubs`, `spatial_transitions`, `lisa_transitions`, `inequality`, `spatial_model`, `spatial_diagnostics`, `mgwr`, and on `aggregate`. It defaults to the data's own map: `geo.load()` records it in `df.attrs["geo:scale"]`, pandas keeps it through filtering, and a dataset id brings its own. A table whose units are on several maps and that does not record which (a merge of datasets, for instance) raises an error asking for `map=`.
- `geo.map()`'s `scale=` argument is now `map=`, and `convergence_clubs(map=False)` is now `draw_map=False`.
- Results name the map in their description of the weights: `w_spec` ends in "(on map343)".
- `geo.scale_of()` raises for an ID that is on several maps; `geo.change()`, `geo.combine()` and `geo.aggregate()` keep or set the map of the table they return.
- **Building and validating:** `publish_geo` and `from_polygons` accept maps that share IDs (`from_polygons(..., scale=)`); `validate` allows IDs shared by scales with the same pattern, checks a map that nests by ID only (`nesting: ids` in `scales.yaml`) with a looser geometric test, and checks every other crosswalk in `geo/crosswalks/`.
- **Older versions:** geo4bolivia 0.7.2 and earlier read the old layout, so they no longer work with the current data. Upgrade (`pip install -U geo4bolivia`), or keep them working with `ref="v0.7.2"` (or `GEO4BOLIVIA_REF=v0.7.2`), which reads the data as they were at that release.

## 0.7.2 (2026-11-20)

**Maps: the basemap's credit moves off the map.** The white "© OpenStreetMap contributors © CARTO" box no longer covers a corner of every map drawn on a basemap (`map`, `lisa`, `connectivity`, `lisa_transitions`, `mgwr`, `convergence_clubs`, ...): the same CARTO style is drawn without its box, and the credit the tiles' licences require is a small grey line below the map. The style is downloaded from CARTO once per session; without a connection the maps keep Plotly's box. On this site the credit is a small (i) button on the map.

## 0.7.1 (2026-11-20)

**`lisa`: a larger cluster map.** In the two-panel figure the map now takes a little more width than the Moran scatterplot (56% and 44%) and its view is fitted to its panel, so Bolivia is drawn about 45% larger while the whole country stays in view; the figure is a little taller (650 px). The clusters, counts and reading are unchanged.

## 0.7.0 (2026-11-20)

**`lisa` shows the Moran scatterplot and the cluster map side by side.** `.fig` is now one interactive figure with both panels and one legend: a click on a type (High-High, Low-Low, the outliers, not significant) shows or hides it on the scatterplot and on the map at once. `panels="map"` or `panels="scatter"` gives one panel alone, and the result keeps each one as `.fig_map` (new) and `.fig_scatter`. Nothing else changes: the same clusters, counts and reading.

**Documentation**

- The site opens in a dark theme matching the observatory's website (a toggle switches to light), with dark figures and tables. Every code box has Copy at the top and, for Python, Open in Colab at the bottom, which opens the page's notebook; each function of the reference has its own example notebook.
- A night-sky background (faint stars over a blue-to-teal gradient, fixed while the page scrolls), shared with the observatory's website.

## 0.6.0 (2026-11-20)

geo4bolivia becomes a self-contained package for spatial data science, in its own repository, with its own documentation site.

**New: the analyses are built in.** Every function below takes a dataset id or a panel with `geo_id` and `year`, finds the boundaries, the spatial weights and the labels itself, and returns a result object with `.df`, `.fig` (Plotly), `.gt` (a table, where one helps) and `.interpret()`, a reading of the numbers in words.

| Family | Functions |
| --- | --- |
| Explore | `correlation`, `extremes`, `distribution`, `scatter`, `trend` |
| Maps | `map` gains class schemes (`scheme="fisher_jenks"`, `"quantiles"`, `"equal_interval"`, or `bins=`), several years side by side in common classes, and `change=True` |
| Spatial dependence | `weights`, `connectivity`, `moran`, `lisa` |
| Convergence | `beta_convergence` (ordinary and spatial models), `sigma_convergence`, `convergence_clubs` |
| Transitions and mobility | `transitions`, `spatial_transitions`, `lisa_transitions`, `rank_mobility` |
| Inequality | `inequality` (Gini, Theil, coefficient of variation, Lorenz curve), `theil_decomposition` |
| Models | `regression`, `panel_model` (with the Hausman test), `spatial_model`, `spatial_diagnostics` |
| Spatial heterogeneity | `mgwr` (multiscale geographically weighted regression) |

The analysis engine is ported from the sister package [geometrics](https://quarcs-lab.github.io/geometrics/), and the exploration functions and panel models follow [expdpy](https://cmg777.github.io/expdpy/). Both remain the place for specialised methods; `for_geometrics` and `for_expdpy` still hand panels over to them.

**Changed**

- **Two repositories.** The package now lives in [quarcs-lab/geo4bolivia](https://github.com/quarcs-lab/geo4bolivia). The data, their builders, the notebooks and the observatory website moved to [quarcs-lab/gdo4bolivia](https://github.com/quarcs-lab/gdo4bolivia), which the package reads.
- **Versions 0.5 and earlier no longer find the data**, because they look for them at the package's old address. Upgrade with `pip install -U geo4bolivia`. If you cannot upgrade, set the environment variable `GEO4BOLIVIA_BASE_URL` to `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/quarcs-lab/gdo4bolivia/{ref}/`.
- **Dependencies.** The default install now includes the libraries of the core analyses: libpysal, esda, spreg, inequality, mapclassify, statsmodels, scipy, plotly and great-tables. Heavier ones are extras: `geo4bolivia[dynamics]` (giddy, for `transitions` and `spatial_transitions`), `[mgwr]` (for `mgwr`), `[panel]` (linearmodels, for `panel_model`), `[raster]` (rasterio, for `zonal`) and `[all]`. `[plot]` is kept as an empty alias, since plotly is now always installed.
- **`geo4bolivia build`** runs the builders from the `builders/` folder of a checkout of the data repository; the package keeps only the generic build helpers.

## 0.5.0 (2026-11-17)

Functions to understand the data: `search`, `info`, `reference_years`, `cite`, `labels`, `describe`, `add_names`, `change` and `map`; `load` with names and groups; aggregation to several scales with coverage; census-population-weighted aggregation of the SDG Atlas indicators.

## 0.4.0 (2026-11-10)

The SDG Atlas 2026 (two periods, 15 goals, 81 indicators) on SDSN Bolivia's map of 343 municipalities and indigenous autonomies.

## 0.3.0 and earlier

The first releases: the scale registry and geo IDs, loading, linking, aggregation, zonal statistics, and the bridges to geometrics and expdpy.
